question: A convex lens forms a real and inverted image twice the size of the object. The magnification produced by the lens is equal to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnification (m)** is defined as the **ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object**.
 
• For a real and inverted image, the magnification is given a negative sign.
 
• In this case, the image is twice the size of the object, hence the magnification is **-2**.
 
• The formula for magnification (m) is: **m = - (Image Height) / (Object Height)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The lens formula is given by **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**, where **f** is the focal length, **v** is the image distance, and **u** is the object distance.
 
• In this problem, knowing the magnification helps in understanding the relationship between the object and image distances.
 
• **Convex lenses can produce both real and virtual images** depending on the position of the object relative to the focal point.
